learning: Hypotheses: (1) at y = 0.075 m, line loss falls because of the longer reaction distance; (2) kd 0.4 keeps oscillation near 0.2 without losing response; (3) if line loss is 0 but max_error stays at or above 0.06, the limit is turning authority (narrower wheel_track). Measuring line_loss_events per track separates sensor coverage from control, and steering_oscillation tests whether kd is still damping.
notes: Runs the Builder's y = 0.075 m array, which follows the line-loss rule. Only kd changes (0.3 to 0.4) to damp the rising steering oscillation from the forward array (0.20 to 0.24 in iteration 3). Speed and gains are otherwise held so the result is readable.
rationale: Iteration 3 (array at y = 0.065 m, 50 mm span, controller unchanged) scored 82.8. Line loss did not clear: 2.0 events on the oval, 2.0 on the s-bend and 1.7 on the slalom. Max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.066, still above the 0.06 m off-track floor, and no run finished. Steering oscillation rose to 0.20 to 0.24, which is the jitter cost of moving the array forward. My earlier rule says to move the array to about y = 0.075 m while line loss is still at least 1 per track, and the Builder's geometry does this, so I keep it. Because the score is about 147 times progress at this loss level, the lever that matters is getting further along the track before leaving it. The added jitter is the main new risk, so I raise kd from 0.3 to 0.4 to damp the faster-changing signal from the forward array. kp (4.0), ki (0.1), base_speed (1.4) and last_direction line loss are kept, so the kd change is the only controller variable moved. Expected result: steering_oscillation falls back toward 0.15 to 0.2, line_loss_events falls toward 0 or stays near 2, and progress rises above the iteration-3 values (0.27, 0.21, 0.14). I do not claim this outcome. Speed is held because no run has finished and the speed margin is still unproven.
